deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is a continuous prose passage from Riemann's natural-philosophical/psychological fragments, edited by Weber and Dedekind in the Gesammelte Werke (1876) among the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts', in the 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik' material. The theory is Herbartian and Fechnerian.

(1) It continues the 'laws of mental processes' (Gesetze geistiger Vorgänge) about 'Geistesmassen' (mental masses) begun on the previous page:
- Every newly forming Geistesmasse enters into immediate interaction (Wechselwirkung) with the Geistesmassen formed just before it.
- Mediately, all older Geistesmassen connected with those are stimulated to activity. The stimulation is weaker the more remotely they are connected and the less they hang together among themselves. This is a qualitative spreading-activation law that decreases with connection distance; no formula is given.
- The formation of new masses depends partly on older masses and partly on external (material) causes.
- The most general and simplest manifestation of an old mass's activity is 'reproduction': it strives to produce something similar to itself.
- Everything acting jointly or simultaneously inhibits or furthers itself according to the inner dissimilarity or similarity of the Geistesmassen it strives to produce. The marginal query '((gleichzeitige?))' weighs 'gemeinschaftlich' against 'gleichzeitig'. This is Herbart's Hemmung/Verschmelzung idea, stated qualitatively.

(2) After a horizontal rule, section '3. (Erdseele)' (pencil heading) begins:
- These laws, derived from the explanation of inner perception, are to be applied to explain the purposiveness (Zweckmässigkeit) observed on Earth, i.e. the existence and historical development of organisms.
- It recapitulates the premises: Geistesmassen produced in nerve processes persist unchanged as parts of the soul and change only by entering new combinations.
- A parenthetical gives the only quantitative statement: a Geistesmasse that appears simple to us is produced in a nerve process lasting about 1/10 to 1/9 of a second, in a single primitive nerve fibre (Primitivfaser).
- The page ends mid-sentence. The claim is that the souls of organisms persist after death; this is completed on the next page and leads to the 'Erdseele'.

No computations are present. The only number is the empirical time constant of 0.100 to 0.111 s.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics on the page.
The sentence 'Wenden wir nun diese Gesetze ... und der geschichtlichen Entwicklung' is grammatically incomplete: the separable particle 'an' of 'anwenden' is missing. This is a drafting slip.

The 1/10–1/9 s duration for an elementary nerve process is an empirical estimate. It is plausible as an order of magnitude for the psychophysics of the 1850s (cf. Helmholtz's nerve-conduction measurements and reaction-time work), but it is not justified on the page.

results.what: Qualitative law of mediated activation of older 'Geistesmassen', decreasing with associative distance, plus mutual inhibition or facilitation by dissimilarity or similarity
results.modern_name: Associationist psychology / spreading activation; Herbartian inhibition (Hemmung) and fusion (Verschmelzung) of presentations
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart (Psychologie als Wissenschaft, 1824–25); spreading activation in modern form: Collins & Loftus (1975)

results.what: Application of psychological laws to a world-soul ('Erdseele') to explain purposiveness in organic nature
Estimate that an elementary (simple-seeming) mental act corresponds to a nerve process of about 1/10–1/9 s in one primitive fibre
results.modern_name: Psychological moment / temporal resolution of perception (~100 ms)
results.usually_credited_to: Later psychophysics (e.g. K. E. von Baer's 'moment' 1860; J. Stroud's 'perceptual moment' 1955)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the known natural-philosophy fragment on Geistesmassen and the Erdseele, published by Weber and Dedekind in Riemann's Werke. It is Herbartian/Fechnerian in content, with no mathematics. The ~100 ms estimate is mildly interesting but already in print.

checkable.asserts: The stated duration range 1/10–1/9 s has width 1/90 s (~11 ms).
The elementary nerve process lasts about 0.100 to 0.111 seconds.

transcription_corrections: The page number '26.' and the pencil folio number '13' in the margin near section 3 are confirmed by the image.
The pencil heading reads '3. ——— (Erdseele)'. It is a later, faint pencil addition beside the start of the new section.
The faint pencil marginal note after the first section, rendered '[?]', appears to read something like 'bei sachen ||'. It is illegible or uncertain.
The marginal query is indeed '(( gleichzeitige? ))', written opposite 'gemeinschaftlich'.
Line 'Wenden wir nun diese Gesetze geistiger Vorgänge,' is correct as written. The verb particle 'an' is missing in the manuscript itself, not a transcription error.
